insecureContext.headline: Page is not secure — without HTTPS there is no camera
lines: On http:// or when the browser shows “Not secure”, camera and microphone are blocked. This is not a Diebel bug.
Open the same site with https:// and the padlock in the address bar, then try the video call again.
If you added a home screen icon: remove it, open the site in the browser on https, then add it again.

securityError.headline: The browser blocks the camera or microphone (security)
lines: Often happens without https:// or when the site has no permission. Check the padlock in the address bar.
In Chrome/Edge: padlock → Site permissions → Camera and Microphone → Allow.
After changing: tap “Try again” or restart the call.

overconstrained.headline: Camera or microphone is busy / does not support the requested settings
linesLocalhost: This can happen even if you already tapped “Allow” — it is not always a permission denial.
Close other video calls, Zoom, Discord, or apps using the camera or microphone, then tap “Try again”.
On some phones: reload the page after freeing the camera.
On http://localhost, Edge’s “connection isn’t secure” is about HTTP; it does not mean your “Microphone: Allowed” list is wrong.
linesRemote: This can happen even if you already tapped “Allow” — it is not always a permission denial.
Close other video calls, Zoom, Discord, or apps using the camera or microphone, then tap “Try again”.
On some phones: reload the page after freeing the camera.
If you are not on localhost, use https:// for this site — otherwise the browser may block camera and microphone.

notFoundLocalhost.headline: No microphone or camera found on this PC
lines: The popup may say “Allowed”, but the system exposes no device to the browser.
Windows: Settings → Privacy → Microphone → allow desktop apps access.
In Edge: open edge://settings/content/microphone and check that the microphone is not blocked globally.

notAllowedLocalhost.headline: The list says “Allow”, but the browser still refuses the microphone
lines: On http://localhost this is NOT from the red “Not secure” banner — you can have microphone “Allowed” while the page is “not secure”.
Check edge://settings/content/microphone (global blocks, InPrivate, corporate policies).
Try closing Teams / Discord / OBS / other tabs with camera, then “Try again”.
As a test: open the same URL in Chrome or a clean Edge profile.

localhostGeneric.headline: Localhost: “Not secure” in Edge ≠ “your microphone is blocked”
lines: At http://localhost:3005 it is normal to see an HTTP security warning; Chrome/Edge still treat localhost as an origin where media APIs are allowed.
If Microphone and Camera are “Allowed” for the site, next free the device: close other calls or apps using it.
Tap “Try again” or hard-reload with Ctrl+F5. If it still fails, note the console error (F12) so we can reproduce.
Testing from a phone on the same PC: do not use http://IP — use https on a domain or a tunnel (ngrok); on insecure IP, mobile blocks media.

default.notAllowedHeadline: The browser blocks the microphone or camera
lines: The browser must allow microphone and camera for this site (1:1 calls and conference use the same permissions).
Desktop: padlock or “i” next to the address → Microphone and Camera → “Allow”.
Android (Chrome): site menu → Permissions → Microphone / Camera.
iPhone (Safari): Settings → Safari → microphone / camera access for the site.
After changing: “Try again” here or restart the call. In production always use https://.
